relevance_note: Retrospective NIH cohort of 38 SAID patients on combination therapy; Table 5 gives row-level data for six patients whose SAID is 'PAPA' (e.g. '| 4 | PAPA | ADA+CAN+RUX | PG |'), though no PSTPIP1 variant or gene is named anywhere in the paper.
method_note: In-scope people are the six Table 5 rows whose SAID column reads 'PAPA' (Pt # 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11), labelled 'Table 5 #<n>' because the 'Pt #' column holds bare index numbers. Table 5 lists only patients with infectious episodes; other PAPA patients in the cohort (Table 3 and Supplementary Table 1 are not available in the converted text) cannot be identified. Pt #12 (SAID 'PASH') was left out: the paper never ties PASH or any patient to PSTPIP1, and calling PASH part of the PSTPIP1 spectrum would rely on outside knowledge. No variant rows: the paper names no gene and prints no variant for any patient; the cohort was described as 'genetically confirmed SAIDs as well as undifferentiated' but no individual PAPA patient is stated to have a PSTPIP1 variant, so variant rows with 'not reported' were not created. n_patients_reported left null (no stated count of PSTPIP1 carriers). Group-level PAPA statements (three PAPA cases needing a JAK inhibitor; secondary loss of efficacy in 6 PAPA patients) were not assigned to individuals. The ACT indication column (PG, NCA, Arthritis) was taken as an observed feature of that patient. Osteomyelitis in Pt #9 is listed as an infection, so the checklist item 'sterile osteomyelitis' was left not reported. 'Recurrent infections' was marked observed only where the cell says 'Recurrent' or 'Episodes of'. A 'No' in the pre-ACT infections column (Pt #4) was not used to exclude anything. The table was transcribed by a short script from the paper rows; every value was checked against the table.
